messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Portuguese, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Portuguese line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table (Step 3)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (truth‑conditions) | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|-------------------------------------------|----------------------|------------------------|--------| | ove | locative adverb introducing a place where the following event occurs | onde | “where” | OK | | udirai | future action of the addressee: will hear the following noun | ouvirás | “you will hear” | OK | | le | definite article, fem. pl., marks *strida* as specific | os | “the” (masc. pl.) | OK | | disperate | adjective qualifying *strida* as expressing desperation | desesperados | “desperate” | OK | | strida | plural noun, the audible objects that will be heard | gritos | “shouts / cries” | OK | | vedrai | future action of the addressee: will see the following noun phrase | verás | “you will see” | OK | | li | definite article, masc. pl., marks *spiriti* as specific | os | “the” (masc. pl.) | OK | | antichi | adjective, temporal attribute of *spiriti*; they belong to an earlier age | antigos | “ancient” | OK | | spiriti | plural noun, the entities that will be seen | espíritos | “spirits” | OK | | dolenti | adjective describing the emotional state of the *spiriti*; woeful | dolorosos | “woeful / sorrowful” | OK | | ch' (che) | relative pronoun referring back to *spiriti*, introduces clause describing their action | que | “who / that” | OK | | a | preposition marking direction toward *morte* | à* | “to/toward” (combined with article) | OK | | la | definite article, fem. sg., marks *morte* as specific | (part of “à”) | “the” (fem.) | OK | | seconda | ordinal adjective, specifies a particular death distinct from the first | segunda | “second” | OK | | morte | noun, the target toward which each spirit shouts | morte | “death” | OK | | ciascun | distributive pronoun, each individual spirit performs the action | cada um | “each one” | OK | | grida | present‑tense verb (3rd sg.) describing the action of shouting toward the second death | grita | “shouts / cries out” | OK |
\* In Portuguese the preposition **a** + article **a** contracts to **à**; the translation therefore renders the two Italian tokens *a* + *la* as the single form **à**.
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **None.** All source tokens are represented in the Portuguese translation, and no grammatical mismatches, missing elements, or unnecessary insertions were detected.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Portuguese script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Portuguese text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
